security_audit.summary: The real security exposure is intentional use of the belt CLI to run remote AI media jobs and install related CLI skills. Many static findings are markdown or placeholder URLs, but the skill still needs clear warnings about external processing and synthetic-media consent.

remediation.suggestion: Keep tool permissions limited to belt commands and explain that examples call remote inference.sh services. Avoid unnecessary npx install commands inside the skill body.
Tell users that images, audio, scripts, and videos may be uploaded to external model providers. Warn users not to submit private or unlicensed media.
Add consent and disclosure guidance for avatar videos, UGC ads, virtual influencers, and voice-driven likeness workflows.

content.value_statement: Teams need fast avatar videos without rebuilding each media workflow. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through belt CLI commands for talking heads, lipsync, and dubbing.
actual_capabilities: Recommends avatar video models for speed, cost, quality, and built-in text-to-speech support.
Shows belt CLI workflows for portrait-to-video, audio-driven avatars, and lipsync videos.
Combines image generation, speech generation, transcription, translation, and video synchronization steps.
Supports use cases for product demos, education, localization, social content, corporate updates, and games.
Provides command examples for P-Video-Avatar, OmniHuman, Fabric, PixVerse, Kokoro, and LatentSync.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an account with access to the selected models.
Runs remote AI media jobs, so private or restricted media should not be submitted without approval.
Output quality depends on portrait framing, audio clarity, model limits, and provider availability.
The skill does not verify likeness rights, advertising compliance, or disclosure requirements.

use_cases.title: Produce Short Product Demos
use_cases.description: Create a talking presenter from a product script and a prepared portrait for campaign videos.

use_cases.title: Localize Training Videos
use_cases.description: Transcribe, translate, generate new speech, and lipsync an existing video for another language.

use_cases.title: Prototype Game Dialogue
use_cases.description: Generate avatar clips for character previews, NPC dialogue, and narrative tests.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Basic Avatar Clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 20 second avatar video from my portrait and script. Use the simplest model with built-in text-to-speech.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Avatar Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the available avatar models for my use case. Prioritize cost, speed, built-in voice support, and expected quality.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Dubbing Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Translate and lipsync an existing video
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a dubbing workflow for this source video. Include transcription, translation, speech generation, lipsync, and review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Scale Variant Production
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a batch workflow for three presenters, two scripts, and two voice styles. Include naming, consent checks, and quality review steps.

output_examples.input: A marketer asks for a vertical avatar ad using one portrait and a short script.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends P-Video-Avatar, selects a voice, sets vertical output, and prepares a belt CLI run plan.

output_examples.input: A training team asks to dub a short internal video into another language.
output: Run lipsync with the original video.

output_examples.input: A studio wants several presenter variants for a game dialogue test.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests a batch workflow with different voices, approved portraits, consistent naming, and manual quality checks.

best_practices: Use portraits and voices only when you have clear permission from the rights holder.
Review scripts for disclosure, brand safety, factual accuracy, and audience requirements before generation.
Test short clips first to confirm framing, voice tone, timing, and model cost.
anti_patterns: Do not generate a real person likeness without consent or a valid legal basis.
Do not submit private customer media, unreleased assets, or regulated data to remote models.
Do not publish synthetic testimonials without clear review and required disclosure.

faq.question: Does this skill generate videos locally?
faq.answer: No. It guides belt CLI commands that run remote inference.sh model jobs.

faq.question: Which model should beginners start with?
faq.answer: The skill recommends P-Video-Avatar because it includes text-to-speech and needs fewer workflow steps.

faq.question: Can it use my own audio file?
faq.answer: Yes. Several workflows accept an audio URL for lipsync or audio-driven avatar generation.

faq.question: Can it create translated avatar videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines transcription, translation, speech generation, and lipsync steps for dubbing workflows.

faq.question: What media quality matters most?
faq.answer: Use clear front-facing portraits, clean audio, accurate scripts, and short test clips before final production.

faq.question: What safety checks are needed?
faq.answer: Confirm consent, disclosure rules, brand approval, and external processing approval before publishing avatar videos.
